title: How the World Learned to Live with the Exclusion of Afghan Women
gist: Five years after the Taliban's return, Afghanistan remains the only country on earth barring girls and women from secondary and higher education, with more than 2 million adolescent girls denied schooling alongside exclusion from workplaces and expanding limits on movement, expression and participation.

insights.claim: Afghanistan is the only country in the world where girls and women are prohibited from accessing secondary and higher education, with more than 2 million adolescent girls denied the right to continue learning.
insights.speaker: Murwarid Ziayee
insights.so_what: A cohort of 2 million-plus girls locked out of schooling is a permanent hit to Afghan human capital and labor supply - it hard-caps any medium-term development or reconstruction case.
insights.quote: Afghanistan remains the only country in the world where girls and women are prohibited from accessing secondary and higher education.
insights.locator: Today, girls have been banned from secondary schools

insights.claim: The author argues the Taliban's 2021 return marked the start of a systematic effort to remove Afghan women and girls from public life, not merely a change of government.
insights.speaker: Murwarid Ziayee
insights.so_what: Framing the policy as systematic rather than incidental implies it is not reversible through diplomatic engagement alone - discount scenarios that assume gradual liberalization.
insights.quote: the fall of Afghanistan was the beginning of a systematic effort to remove them from public life and rob an entire generation of their future
insights.locator: Five years ago, when the Taliban returned

insights.claim: Restrictions have expanded beyond education to workplaces, movement, expression and participation in society, indicating the exclusion regime has broadened over five years rather than stabilized.
insights.speaker: Murwarid Ziayee
insights.so_what: Widening rather than static restrictions argue against normalization of relations and keep aid and recognition constrained.
insights.locator: women have been pushed out of workplaces
